life_summary: Joshua Reuben Clark Jr. was born September 1, 1871, in Grantsville, Utah Territory, to parents of English and Swiss descent. A voracious student and ambitious intellectual, he excelled academically at the University of Utah before pursuing advanced legal training at Columbia University Law School. His distinguished career in international diplomacy included service as Assistant Solicitor and Solicitor in the U.S. State Department, Under-Secretary of State under President Calvin Coolidge, and U.S. Ambassador to Mexico (1930–1933). Clark authored the influential Clark Memorandum, which reinterpreted the Monroe Doctrine and established him as a major figure in twentieth-century American foreign policy. He navigated elite academic, diplomatic, and governmental circles with distinction before redirecting his energies toward full-time Church service.
church_summary: In 1933, Clark was called to the First Presidency as Second Counselor to President Heber J. Grant and was ordained an apostle in 1934. He served as Second Counselor under George Albert Smith (1945–1951) and as First Counselor under David O. McKay (1951–1959, 1959–1961), accumulating over 28 years of service in the Church's highest councils. His presidency focused on character-building through welfare initiatives and defending the Church's institutional independence from state interference. His published works, including Our Lord of the Gospels and Why the King James Version, reflected his intellectual rigor and spiritual depth. He modeled the integration of worldly expertise and ecclesiastical authority, demonstrating that the Church could benefit from leaders educated in secular excellence.
teaching_emphasis: Legal and constitutional defense of Church interests
